item.title: Good Ghouls Gone Bad: Halloween Pole Showcase — Sat Oct 17, 5:30 PM — Euphoria Davis Pole Studio
item.description:
Join us for our second Annual Halloween-themed showcase at Euphoria Pole Studio! Come cheer on our wonderful students and instructors as we spook our way around the stage! There will be pole dancing, belly dancing, doubles and group performances, murder, clowns, and inner demons. We invite all of YOU to dress up too! Come in your spookiest and Halloweeniest attire! There will be light snacks and refreshments, an audience competition intermission, and pole-tergeists.

item.title: Davis High Theater Presents: The Tragedy of Macbeth — Sat Oct 17, 7:00 PM — Richard Brunelle Performance Hall
item.description: If you knew you were destined for power, would you let fate take its course or would you grab destiny by the wheel and hit the gas? When three mysterious witches awaken Macbeth’s hunger for power, ambition sets in motion a bloody chain of betrayal, murder, and madness. Shakespeare’s iconic, haunting tragedy explores the dangerous consequences of mistaking destiny for something we can control. Location Brunelle Theater @ 315 W 14th Street. Performances Friday, October 16, Saturday October 17, Friday October 23, Saturday October 24 @7:00PM Sunday October 18 and Sunday October 25 @2:00PM Tickets $15 general admission, $10 for DJUSD students, and $5 on Sundays for DJUSD students. You can buy your tickets online at https://sites.google.com/view/davishightheatre/home We also encourage bringing cash for concessions ($2 each) to avoid an online fee. We hope to see you there! Any questions, please contact Shenandoah Kehoe skehoe@djusd.net Image courtesy of Chad Fisk Joseph Martin as Macb

item.title: Live Band Karaoke — Sat Oct 17, 7:30 PM — Comasocial
item.description:

Not much of a singer? Don’t worry! Jump on stage and rock out with the band with a guitar controller! No experience required to participate. 🎵 700+ songs spanning classic rock, pop, alternative, metal, and more. No experience? No problem! Everyone is welcome. item.description: It’s 1987 on Los Angeles’ legendary Sunset Strip, where the Bourbon Room is the heart of the rock-and-roll scene. It’s part rock concert, part comedy, part love letter to the ’80s…and completely ready to rock your socks off!!! item.title: Davis Craft and Vintage Fair — Sun Oct 18, 10:00 AM — Central Park – Davis
item.description:
Davis Craft and Vintage Fair began as the Square Tomatoes Craft Fair more than 10 years ago! The event was started by instructors from the UC Davis Craft Center in order to have a monthly craft fair for local artisans and the local community. We embraced local vintage vendors in 2017, we’ve grown and we are still home to local artists and makers from the Davis and greater Sacramento area. We collaborate with local non-profits starting with Couleurs Vives Art Studio who joined us in 2018! Many of our talented vendors can be found at other festivals like the Davis Phoenix Coalition’s Pride Fest, the I-House’s International Festival, and 2nd Friday ArtAbouts on E Street Plaza. Expect to see friendly vendors with local handmade and original art, crafts, quality vintage items, upcycled treasures, earth-friendly creations, good food, and more. Free live music fills the open space for a lively atmosphere so be sure to stop by and join us!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Birds & Bikes — Sun Oct 18, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: Axis Gallery is proud to announce Birds & Bikes, a collaborative art exhibition bringing together regional artists to explore the poetic intersections of avian flight and human motion. Running from October 2 through November 1, 2026, the exhibition showcases a dynamic range of works from intricate metal sculptures and imaginative textile art to curated gallery shop goods, celebrating the beauty of migration alongside the engineering of daily travel. The exhibition features a direct partnership with the City of Sacramento Office of Arts and Culture (OAC) Art in Public Places program and North Natomas Jibe. Birds & Bikes serves as an artistic tie-in to the upcoming Birds and Benches project, which will install artist-designed public benches across North Natomas Regional Park. Visitors are invited to experience the unique ecology and transit identity of the Natomas Basin through a collaborative lens, discover one-of-a-kind art pieces, and browse handcrafted items in the East Gallery Pop

item.description: Get ready to celebrate those who give back and make a difference at the Yolo Philanthropy Awards 2026! About the Yolo Philanthropy Awards Yolo Community Foundation (YCF) hosts the annual Awards celebration as a way for nonprofits to honor and celebrate volunteers and donors who make a big difference in our community, without each nonprofit needing to spend the time and resources to host their own events. Please join us for the annual Yolo Philanthropy Awards, sponsored by Nugget Markets, as we celebrate and honor those who make a significant impact in Yolo County. 43 local nonprofits are coming together to recognize volunteers and donors who make our community a better place. item.title: Davis City Council Meetings — Thu Jan 14, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change.
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance.
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.

item.title: Making Sense of Scientific Articles: A Survival Kit for Reading Research Papers — Wed Oct 28, 2:30 PM — Shields Library
item.description:
Struggling to make sense of scientific papers? You're not alone! Scientific articles can be intimidating, but knowing how to approach them makes a big difference.
Join students from the College of Biological Sciences' BioInnovation Group for a workshop designed to help you tackle scientific papers with confidence. Learn how to find research articles that interest you, navigate the different sections of a scientific paper, and break down complex research into your own words. We'll share practical tips and tricks to make reading scientific literature feel a little less overwhelming.
Whether you're reading papers for a class, exploring a research topic, or just curious about scientific discoveries, this workshop will help you build skills you can use throughout your academic journey.
Source: UC Davis Library

item.title: Davis Farmers Market – Wednesday Evenings (50th Anniversary Year) — Wed Dec 30, 3:00 PM — Central Park
item.description:
The Davis Farmers Market continues every Wednesday in Central Park with new fall hours! Beginning Wednesday, September 2, the Wednesday market will be open from 3:00–6:00 PM, replacing the extended 4:00–8:00 PM Picnic in the Park hours. Stop by to shop for fresh, locally grown produce, artisan goods, prepared foods and other market favorites from local farmers and vendors. It’s a great opportunity to stock up for the week, meet up with friends, support local growers and food makers, and enjoy a beautiful afternoon in Central Park. The Davis Farmers Market is celebrating its 50th Anniversary in 2026, marking five decades of bringing fresh food, local farmers and the Davis community together. Wednesday Market Details:
Wednesdays from 3:00–6:00 PM Central Park in Downtown Davis Fresh, seasonal produce Artisan goods and prepared foods Local farmers and food makers Family-friendly and open to everyone
Free to attend – shop local and enjoy your Wednesday afternoon at the Davis Farmers

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Dec 30, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants
